x: Henry Martin managed to dodge all offers to join the Army and scored a triple win in the 100, 220 and 440. George Davidson ran sensibly to win the 1 mile and some anonymous vocal support spurred Dave Hooper into 2nd place.
George Davidson although faced with tough opposition, ran well to finish 6th in the half mile, whilst Peter Bagnall lacking the necessary fast finish, recorded 4th in the mile in 4m.20s.
We missed Ray Tooby - who failed to make an appearance - in the 880 yards, but George Davidson carried our colours and came 5th. Jon Burr did not run with his usual zest and did not gain a point.
Heathfield finished 1st in 50.5s. with G.
Jack Brown is to be congratulated on once again getting his name inscribed on the trophy as also are Eddie Short and George Davidson on their 2nd and 3rd placings.
Boreham (380 yards) was a comfortable winner in 9mins. 12secs. There was a terrific tussle for the placings, G. Davidson (150 yds) putting in a well judged finish to beat E.
5. · G. Davidson · 56. 7
George Davidson ran well on the 4th section and put us even further in front. Poly through an excellent run by Richards, moved up to second followed by Herne Hill.
These four opened up a short gap from George Davidson. When the second lap of the Common was completed, Walker was again leading and Flanagan was beginning to feel the effects of the fast pace.

George Davidson, also a first timer, had little or nothing to make his effort worthwhile for we were over a minute behind the nearest club, however he was anxious to prove his team selection and his time of 17.40 was the fastest of the day.
In the 440 yards Dudley Gordon finished 2nd; John Davis won the 880 yards with George Davidson fourth. The two miles was won by Dave Baulch with Don Stroud 2nd and Dave Hooper 3rd.
Brian Hallowell won the 880 yards with George Davidson 3rd. We had only one runner in the mile, Steve Boreham, who did his fastest time in finishing 3rd.
The R.A.M.C. were unable to compete in every event, but in winning the 880 yards their runner Baker scored a fine win in 1m.58.5s. closely followed by B. Hallowell and G.
In the 880 heats George Davidson was 5th in 1.58.5 which gained him a Southern standard. Alan Sexton won his heat in 440 in 50.3s but Frank Kemp failed to qualify.
It must be pointed out that if George Davidson had not turned out in the mile and javelin, we should not have had anyone for these events and it is doubtful if we should have retained the trophy.

However, after much persuasion Bill Bird made our three in the 3000 metres team race, but not being at his best he finished well down. Ray Tooby ran well to be placed third (How about that Club Vest Ray?) and George Davidson was fifth.

Came George Davidson and hopes that some of the leeway would be made up as George had run so well in the recent road race. Although by no means disgracing himself,he could make no impression and was forced to give way to Thorpe of St.Albans.The experience should be invaluable to George in the future.
Dabbs, 50 G.
